stem: Valproic acid is used to treat certain types of which brain condition?

options.label: A
options.misconception: None — valproic acid treats certain types of seizures.
options.explanation: Valproic acid treats certain types of seizures and is also used to treat mania in people with bipolar disorder.

options.label: B
options.misconception: Treats any movement-related brain disorder as an anticonvulsant use.
options.explanation: Parkinson disease reflects loss of dopaminergic nigral neurons and is treated with carbidopa-levodopa; valproate can instead cause tremor and parkinsonism.

options.label: C
options.misconception: Confuses demyelinating disease with abnormal neuronal firing.
options.explanation: Multiple sclerosis is immune-mediated demyelination of the central nervous system, treated with disease-modifying immunotherapies, not anticonvulsants.

options.label: D
options.misconception: Misses that valproate can cause, not treat, hyperammonemic encephalopathy.
options.explanation: Hepatic encephalopathy from ammonia buildup is treated with lactulose and rifaximin; valproate can itself raise ammonia levels.

options.label: E
options.misconception: Treats a CSF-flow disorder as responsive to a neuronal stabilizer.
options.explanation: Normal pressure hydrocephalus causes gait change, incontinence and dementia and is treated by CSF shunting, not an anticonvulsant.

context: Learning objective: Valproic acid treats certain types of seizures and also mania in people with bipolar disorder.
